candidates.title: Newborn Screening for X-Linked Adrenoleukodystrophy: A Systematic Literature Review.
candidates.abstract: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD) is the most common leukodystrophy and peroxisomal disorder. It was added to newborn screening (NBS) programs following its first implementation in New York in 2013. Since then, X-ALD screening has expanded rapidly, although important differences exist among programs. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the global implementation of NBS for X-ALD, including screening methodologies, screening performance, prevalence estimates, genetic findings, and clinical follow-up outcomes. A systematic search of PubMed and EMBASE identified 13 publications describing NBS programs conducted between 2013 and June 2026. All programs used C26:0-lysophosphatidylcholine (C26:0-LPC) as the primary biomarker, although substantial heterogeneity was observed in analytical methodologies, cut-off values, screening algorithms, and follow-up strategies. Positive predictive values ranged from 9.1% to 100%, while screening detection rates varied from 1:3118 to 1:51,081, reflecting differences in study design, screening population, sample size, and screening approaches. Variants of uncertain significance (VUS) accounted for 52.6% of individuals detected with classified ABCD1 variant findings, representing a major challenge for genetic counseling and clinical management. Most identified newborns were asymptomatic at diagnosis, supporting the role of NBS in enabling early surveillance for adrenal insufficiency and cerebral disease before irreversible manifestations occur. In addition, differences between universal and sex-specific screening strategies highlight ongoing clinical and ethical debates regarding the scope of X-ALD NBS. Overall, current evidence supports the feasibility of NBS for X-ALD and its ability to enable presymptomatic ascertainment and early clinical surveillance; however, greater harmonization of screening protocols, improved variant interpretation, and long-term outcome studies are needed to optimize program performance and clinical benefit.

candidates.title: Drivers of Ecosystem Metabolism in an Anthropogenically Modified Delta.
candidates.abstract: Estuaries are under threat globally from a wide range of stressors, with rates of ecosystem metabolism - respiration (R), gross primary production (GPP), and net ecosystem metabolism (NEM) - representing a way for resource managers to quantify their impacts. In this study, we assessed how natural and anthropogenic stressors have altered metabolism within the extensively modified Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta ("Delta") in California, USA. Metabolism was estimated using a diel open-water technique utilizing dissolved oxygen measurements from a high frequency (15 min) water quality monitoring array, and spanned 6 sites across 11 years (2014-2025). Our analyses were driven by a conceptual model of Delta carbon (C) cycling focused on 1) Invasive aquatic vegetation (IAV), 2) Phytoplankton, 3) Wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) upgrades, 4) Large-scale flow alterations, and 5) Wet vs. dry years. We found that allochthonous C fuels net heterotrophy in the outer riverine sections of the Delta, while the heavily vegetated central Delta produces autochthonous C remineralized elsewhere in the system. IAV were the dominant primary producers, with low phytoplankton production except during a historic bloom. WWTP upgrades imparted negligible changes to metabolism, with low chlorophyll a (< 5 µg L-1) both before and after. Introduction of a flow barrier - a management response to drought - hydrodynamically isolated deep-water channels from nearby shallow areas, resulting in decreased metabolism indicative of changes to C transport. Contrary to past research, low rainfall years were associated with increased metabolism. This study demonstrates how multi-sensor arrays can be used to quantify ecosystem responses to major environmental stressors. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s12237-026-01833-z.
candidates.journal: Estuaries and coasts : journal of the Estuarine Research Federation

candidates.title: The Effect of Digital Storytelling on the Anxiety of Patients with Pituitary Adenoma Undergoing Transsphenoidal Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
candidates.abstract: Patients with pituitary adenoma often experience anxiety due to hormonal changes and the stress associated with transsphenoidal surgery. Digital storytelling, as an innovative multimedia-based training method, has recently been used in patient education. This study investigated the effect of digital storytelling on the anxiety of patients with pituitary adenoma undergoing transsphenoidal surgery. This randomized controlled trial was conducted on 70 patients with pituitary adenoma scheduled for transsphenoidal surgery at a teaching hospital affiliated with Tehran University of Medical Sciences. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention or a control group. The intervention group received a 15-20-minute digital storytelling program that included experiences shared by patients and nurses regarding preoperative and postoperative care, while the control group received routine hospital education. Anxiety levels were measured a day before surgery, a day after surgery, and three weeks later using Spielberger's State Anxiety Scale. Data were analyzed by SPSS-25 software using descriptive and inferential statistics. The mean score of anxiety in the intervention group decreased by 12.45 (1.24) units a day after the surgery and by 24.82 (1.32) units three weeks after the surgery compared to baseline (p < 0.001). A significantly lower anxiety level was observed in the intervention group at both post-intervention time periods compared to the pre-intervention time (F = 17.05, p < 0.001). Repeated measures Analysis of Variance confirmed a significant interaction between time and group (F = 25.31, p < 0.001). Digital storytelling was effective in reducing anxiety among patients with pituitary adenoma undergoing transsphenoidal surgery and may serve as a valuable educational intervention.
candidates.journal: Iranian journal of nursing and midwifery research

candidates.title: Progressive Bilateral Weakness Followed by Unilateral Facial Palsy in Guillain-Barré Syndrome Temporally Associated With Multiple Vaccinations.
candidates.abstract: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) is an acute immune-mediated polyradiculoneuropathy in which facial weakness may occur as a cranial neuropathy. Unilateral facial palsy may also prompt a diagnosis of idiopathic Bell's palsy, creating a risk of diagnostic anchoring when broader neurologic symptoms are already present. We report a 32-year-old man with childhood epilepsy who described progressive bilateral upper and lower extremity weakness with paresthesias for approximately two weeks, followed by left facial paralysis about one week later. He also reported co-administration of hepatitis B, influenza, and tetanus vaccines approximately three weeks before presentation; the vaccine products and dates were not independently verified. An outside hospital treated the facial paralysis as presumed Bell's palsy with acyclovir, although the available records do not establish the facial examination pattern, acyclovir regimen, whether corticosteroids were prescribed there, or whether the preceding bilateral limb symptoms were recognized. An outpatient electrodiagnostic study was reportedly interpreted as concerning for GBS, but the complete nerve conduction/electromyography report was unavailable. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) showed white blood cells of 5/mm³, glucose of 59 mg/dL, and protein of 190 mg/dL, supporting albuminocytologic dissociation; a paired serum glucose was unavailable. The patient completed a five-day course of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), and prednisone plus valacyclovir was also documented for the facial palsy, although their exact dose, route, and duration were not recoverable. The source record documented short-term neurologic improvement before discharge. This case emphasizes that unilateral facial palsy should not distract from pre-existing bilateral weakness and paresthesias and that facial weakness in this setting may represent GBS-related cranial neuropathy rather than a separate confirmed Bell's palsy. The temporal association with vaccination does not establish causality.

candidates.title: Postpartum diagnosis of pheochromocytoma presenting as atypical hypertensive disorder of pregnancy: A case report.
candidates.abstract: Pheochromocytoma, a catecholamine-secreting adrenal tumour, is a rare but important cause of hypertension in pregnancy. Its symptoms may mimic more common disorders of pregnancy, making diagnosis challenging. We present a postpartum pheochromocytoma diagnosis with favourable maternal and neonatal outcomes. A 29-year-old woman in her first pregnancy developed proteinuria at 34 weeks and new-onset hypertension at 36 weeks, managed as pre-eclampsia. Worsening hypertension, gestational diabetes and breech presentation led to caesarean section at 36 weeks and 4 days of gestation. Postpartum, she experienced severe headaches, labile blood pressure, tachycardia and sweating. Imaging identified a 4 cm right adrenal mass. Markedly elevated plasma and urinary normetanephrines confirmed pheochromocytoma. Right adrenalectomy was performed seven weeks post-partum, with complete excision. Symptoms resolved postoperatively. Subsequent surveillance imaging showed no recurrence. She later had a second uncomplicated pregnancy. This case highlights how pheochromocytoma in pregnancy can be differentiated from more common conditions. Prompt diagnosis and multidisciplinary management can optimise patient outcomes.

candidates.title: Extradural C1-C2 Dumbbell Schwannoma Mimicking an Intradural Lesion on MRI: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Cervical dumbbell schwannomas are benign nerve sheath tumors that may present diagnostic challenges when preoperative imaging suggests intradural involvement despite an extradural origin. We report the case of a 43‑year‑old African male with a three‑year history of right‑sided cervicobrachialgia and two years of progressive quadriparesis, sensory loss, and mixed reflex abnormalities consistent with cervical myelopathy. MRI demonstrated a 31 × 21 mm C1-C2 mass initially interpreted as intradural‑extramedullary. However, intraoperative findings revealed a purely extradural schwannoma arising from the nerve root, producing significant spinal cord compression through a classic dumbbell configuration. A posterior midline approach with C2 laminectomy allowed safe microsurgical resection, achieving gross total removal without cerebrospinal fluid leakage, without neurological deterioration, and with progressive improvement of quadriparesis. Postoperative MRI confirmed complete resection with expected inflammatory changes and no residual tumor. This case underscores the importance of correlating radiological and intraoperative findings, as cervical schwannomas may mimic intradural lesions on MRI. Accurate classification and tailored surgical planning are essential for optimal outcomes, particularly in resource‑limited settings.

candidates.title: Pegvisomant in severe, treatment-resistant thyroid eye disease: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Teprotumumab, a monoclonal antibody against the IGF1 receptor, has proven effective in the treatment of thyroid eye disease (TED). Pegvisomant reduces IGF1 levels through selective inhibition of growth hormone receptors. Here, we present a hypothesis-generating case of a 69-year-old patient with progressive TED. Pegvisomant 20 mg was administered daily for 90 days. IGF1 levels declined and remained low-normal during treatment. Clinical activity scores and VISA (vision, inflammation, strabismus and appearance) scores improved rapidly. MRI assessment showed that water content of both extraocular muscles and orbital connective tissue decreased after treatment. 99mTc-DTPA SPECT confirmed the decrease in disease activity. Further studies may confirm the efficacy of pegvisomant in TED. A 69-year-old female patient with severe, active thyroid eye disease (TED) – a condition linked to Graves’ disease where the body’s immune system attacks tissues around the eyes – presented with bulging eyes (proptosis), double vision, eye redness, swelling and reduced visual sharpness.Prior treatments with standard therapies for TED, including intravenous steroid courses, radiation therapy targeting the orbit (eye socket) and the biological drug rituximab, failed to achieve improvement. TED progresses in part because proteins called IGF1 receptors on the surface of eye-socket tissues are overactivated. The researchers hypothesized that using pegvisomant, which is a medication typically used for acromegaly (hormone imbalance) that lowers insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) levels in the blood, would reduce activation of these receptors and ease eye inflammation.The patient received a daily 20 mg injection of pegvisomant for 90 days. Symptom improvement The patient experienced a rapid reduction in eye pain, redness and swelling, alongside marked improvement in visual sharpness and colour vision within 8 weeks.MRI and imaging results Orbital MRI and nuclear imaging showed a distinct drop in tissue inflammation and fluid accumulation (oedema) in the muscles around the eye.Proptosis and double vision Eye bulging and double vision did not significantly change during the trial.Safety Pegvisomant was well tolerated with no reported side effects, and her blood sugar and liver function remained stable. Blood IGF1 levels dropped as expected and returned to normal after treatment ended. Pegvisomant rapidly reduced eye inflammation and improved vision in a patient whose TED had resisted standard therapies. However, because this was a single case study, the delayed effects from previous treatments cannot be entirely ruled out. Further clinical trials are needed to determine if pegvisomant is effective at higher doses or when given earlier in the disease course.

candidates.title: Sinonasal and Olfactory Quality of Life Following Endonasal Transsphenoidal Surgery for Pituitary Adenoma: A Multicenter Prospective Cohort Triphasic Recovery Analysis in Ethiopia.
candidates.abstract: To characterize the sinonasal and olfactory quality of life (QoL) trajectory. A multicenter prospective cohort study was conducted on 91 patients undergoing TSS at Addis Ababa University teaching hospitals between May 2024 and August 2025. QoL was evaluated using the Sino-Nasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22) questionnaire v4 preoperatively and at 3- and 6-month postoperatively. Analysis revealed a characteristic triphasic recovery pattern: low preoperative baseline, a transient peak in morbidity at 3 months, and an improvement toward baseline by 6 months for most systemic domains. At 3 months, significant score worsening occurred for loss of smell/taste (mean: 1.7, p < 0.001), thick discharge (mean: 1.0, p < 0.001), congestion (mean: 1.0, p < 0.001), postnasal discharge (mean: 0.7, p < 0.001), and runny nose (mean: 0.5, p = 0.003). By 6 months, persistence was confined to loss of smell/taste (p < 0.001), thick discharge (p < 0.001), and congestion (p = 0.005). Exploratory analysis in the nasoseptal flap cohort (n = 3) showed higher scores. Preliminary findings of delayed ear pain/fullness in acromegaly at 6 months hypothesized to reflect a link between growth hormone normalization and altered Eustachian tube function. Poorer sleep with binostril access (p = 0.017) speculatively associated with bilateral synechiae under limited postoperative care. Unlike Western cohorts, protracted recovery may reflect lack of standardized high-volume saline irrigation and scheduled debridement. TSS demonstrates a favorable long-term QoL profile; however, localized sinonasal and olfactory deficits often persist at 6 months.

candidates.title: Acinetobacter baumannii Nosocomial Meningitis Secondary to Neurosurgical Intervention: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Nosocomial meningitis is a serious complication of neurosurgical procedures, associated with high morbidity and mortality, as well as significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Among the causative pathogens, Acinetobacter baumannii (A. baumannii) is particularly concerning due to its ability to survive for prolonged periods in the hospital environment, its opportunistic virulence, and, especially, its tendency to develop multidrug resistance to antimicrobial agents. Diagnosis is often difficult in the postoperative setting, particularly when the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is altered as a result of the surgical procedure. Rapid identification of the causative agent and early initiation of appropriate antibiotic therapy are essential to limit complications and improve patient prognosis. We report the case of a 27-year-old patient with a history of surgically treated craniopharyngioma complicated by anterior hypopituitarism. Three weeks after surgery, he was admitted to the ICU with suspected postoperative meningitis due to the onset of behavioral disturbances associated with nasal discharge, without a fever. Brain CT was normal. CSF analysis, obtained by lumbar puncture under strict aseptic conditions, revealed a turbid fluid with leukocytosis of 5,760 cells/mm³, predominantly composed of neutrophils, along with elevated protein levels (5.7 g/L) and low glucose levels (0.05 g/L). Direct examination after Gram staining showed Gram-negative coccobacilli with a marked inflammatory reaction. CSF culture grew a multidrug-resistant (MDR) strain of A. baumannii, which was sensitive only to colistin. The patient received antibiotic therapy with colistin, administered intravenously and intrathecally for 18 days, with initial neurological improvement and sterilization of the CSF by the 15th day of treatment. The subsequent course was unfavorable, marked by the development of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to ventilator-associated pneumonia caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), complicated by refractory septic shock, which ultimately led to his death after one month of hospitalization in the ICU. This report highlights the severity of nosocomial meningitis caused by MDR A. baumannii and underscores the importance of implementing infection prevention measures in healthcare settings.

candidates.title: Medullary thyroid carcinoma with pheochromocytoma and cystic parathyroid degeneration in a ret-negative patient: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A (MEN2A) is a rare autosomal dominant hereditary cancer syndrome, predominantly caused by mutations of the RET proto-oncogene on chromosome 10q11.2. It typically presents with medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), pheochromocytoma, and primary hyperparathyroidism. Cases with a MEN2A phenotype but negative RET testing are uncommon, posing challenges for diagnosis and patient management. We report the case of a 63-year-old female who was diagnosed with MTC and pheochromocytoma. and cystic parathyroid gland. Genetic workup was negative for RET proto-oncogene mutations but positive for a heterozygous variant in the TMEM127 tumor suppressor gene. MEN2A is associated with pathogenic germline variants in the RET proto-oncogene in approximately 95-99% of cases. Our patient, however, exhibited a MEN2A-like clinical phenotype in the absence of an identifiable RET mutation, with a pathogenic TMEM127 variant instead. Although TMEM127 is an established susceptibility gene for pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma, its association with the broader MEN2A phenotype remains unclear. This unusual genotype-phenotype discordance raises important questions regarding the potential role of alternative genetic pathways in MEN2-like syndromes and creates uncertainty regarding postoperative surveillance and the appropriate extent of screening and genetic counseling for family members. Our case represents an unusual scenario where the patient presents with a clinical phenotype of MEN2A but is RET negative and positive heterozygous for a variant in the TMEM127. This atypical genetic finding introduces complexities in determining the appropriate follow-up protocol and the scope of familial screening necessary.

candidates.title: Sertoli-Leydig Cell Tumour With Heterologous Elements Presenting as Hyperandrogenaemia and Markedly Elevated Alpha-Fetoprotein: A Challenging Diagnosis.
candidates.abstract: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumours (SLCTs) are rare ovarian sex cord-stromal tumours that classically present with features of virilisation due to androgen excess and are frequently misdiagnosed as polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS). We report a case of a 33-year-old woman with a three-year history of progressive hirsutism, weight gain, and secondary amenorrhoea, initially attributed to PCOS. An incidental pelvic ultrasound arranged in the context of an endocrinology review revealed a large complex solid-cystic mass measuring 21.2 × 13.8 × 23.4 cm. Tumour markers demonstrated a markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) of 8,147 KU/L, raising initial suspicion of a yolk sac (germ cell) tumour. CT imaging confirmed a 23 cm predominantly cystic pelvic mass with no evidence of metastatic disease. Following multi-disciplinary team discussion and referral to a specialist germ cell tumour MDT, the patient underwent laparotomy and left salpingo-oophorectomy. Initial histology reported an immature teratoma; however, following expert second-opinion review by Professor McCluggage, the final diagnosis was revised to a moderately to poorly differentiated SLCT with heterologous intestinal-type mucinous elements and a small carcinoid component. Ascitic fluid cytology demonstrated no malignant cells. This case highlights the risk of anchoring bias in attributing hyperandrogenaemia to PCOS, the capacity of SLCT with heterologous mucinous elements to mimic germ cell tumours biochemically and histologically, and the indispensable role of expert pathological review in rare ovarian tumours.

candidates.title: Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Rebamipide Versus Diquafosol in the Treatment of Dry Eye Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
candidates.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and tolerability of rebamipide (REB) and diquafosol (DQS), two widely used mucin secretagogues, in the treatment of dry eye disease. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Scopus was conducted following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, identifying six comparative studies enrolling 277 patients across South Korea and Japan. Pooled analyses were performed using random-effects models, standardized mean differences (SMDs) for continuous outcomes and risk ratios (RRs) for dichotomous outcomes with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Tear break-up time showed no significant difference between REB and DQS (SMD = -0.21 seconds, 95% CI: -0.52 to 0.11, p=0.20). Subjective symptom scores were also comparable (SMD=0.11, 95% CI: -0.16 to 0.38, p=0.40). Corneal staining scores were nearly identical (SMD=-0.002, 95% CI: -0.324 to 0.321, p=0.993), while conjunctival staining showed a nonsignificant trend favoring REB (SMD=-0.403, 95% CI: -1.508 to 0.702, p=0.475, I²=87.6%). These findings suggest comparable efficacy between both agents as first-line mucin secretagogues in the available studies, though formal equivalence cannot be established from this evidence base, and more large-scale trials are required to validate the findings.

candidates.title: Newly Diagnosed Graves' Disease Followed by the Discovery of a Cavernous Internal Carotid Artery Aneurysm Causing Panhypopituitarism: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Sellar and parasellar vascular lesions are rare causes of pituitary dysfunction and may mimic pituitary adenomas or other sellar masses. Cavernous internal carotid artery (ICA) aneurysms can cause hypopituitarism through compression of the pituitary gland or stalk, but diagnosis may be delayed when symptoms are initially attributed to a more common endocrine disorder. We report a 37-year-old man who presented with six weeks of unintentional weight loss, fatigue, heat intolerance, excessive sweating, anxiety, tremor, and tachycardia. Initial evaluation showed suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), elevated total triiodothyronine (T3), positive thyrotropin receptor antibody, positive thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin, and a hypervascular thyroid gland on ultrasound, consistent with Graves' disease. He was started on methimazole and atenolol. Although thyroid function tests improved, he developed persistent neck discomfort, prompting contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), which revealed an enhancing sellar mass. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed a T2-hypointense sellar lesion with internal flow artifact, and CT angiography confirmed a saccular aneurysm of the cavernous segment of the right ICA. Pituitary hormone evaluation demonstrated secondary adrenal insufficiency, central hypothyroidism, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, growth hormone (GH) deficiency, and mild hyperprolactinemia, consistent with panhypopituitarism from pituitary compression. The patient was started on prednisone and levothyroxine, and atenolol and prednisone were subsequently discontinued before endovascular embolization was performed. At follow-up, symptoms improved, but panhypopituitarism persisted. This case highlights the importance of reassessing patients when endocrine symptoms evolve despite an initially appropriate diagnosis.

candidates.title: Tumor-to-tumor metastasis of colorectal adenocarcinoma within a gonadotroph pituitary adenoma.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary metastases are uncommon, and most cases originate from breast or lung cancer. Tumor-to-tumor metastasis, in which one neoplasm metastasizes into another, is particularly rare in the sellar region. We report a 66-year-old man with metastatic sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma treated with modified FOLFOX6 (5-fluorouracil, L-leucovorin, and oxaliplatin) plus panitumumab; extracranial disease was controlled, whereas a sellar mass initially suspected as a pituitary adenoma slowly enlarged over 2 years. Endocrine testing showed anterior hypopituitarism without arginine vasopressin deficiency. Endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery was performed for continued enlargement and diagnostic uncertainty. Histopathology demonstrated a gonadotroph pituitary adenoma infiltrated by colorectal adenocarcinoma, with extensive intermingling of the 2 components rather than discrete nests, favoring tumor-to-tumor metastasis over a collision tumor. The metastatic component consisted of viable tumor cells without necrosis or convincing treatment effect despite prolonged chemotherapy. This case underscores that metastatic tumor within a pituitary adenoma may enlarge despite favorable systemic therapy outcomes. Metastasis should therefore remain a key differential diagnosis for a sellar mass radiologically suggestive of a pituitary adenoma.

candidates.title: Silymarin attenuates neuroinflammation after subarachnoid hemorrhage by inducing M2 microglial polarization via activation of the JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway.
candidates.abstract: Neuroinflammation represents a key pathological process in early brain injury (EBI) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and contributes significantly to poor outcomes. Silymarin, known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified. An in vivo endovascular perforation model and an in vitro hemoglobin-stimulated model were used to investigate the pharmacological effects of silymarin in SAH. Neurological function was assessed using SAH scores and neurobehavioral scores. Neuronal apoptosis was evaluated by TUNEL staining. Neuroinflammation was measured by ELISA or qPCR, and microglial polarization status was determined by assessing CD86 and CD206 expression via Western blotting (WB) or immunofluorescence (IF) staining. Ruxolitinib and AS1517499 were applied to block the JAK1/STAT6 pathway. Silymarin attenuated early brain injury (EBI) after SAH, as indicated by improved neurological scores, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and lower brain water content. In vivo, silymarin treatment was associated with JAK1/STAT6 activation, elevated M2 markers, and decreased pro‑inflammatory cytokines. In vitro, silymarin activated the JAK1/STAT6 pathway, promoted M2 microglial polarization, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production. In addition, pharmacological blockade of JAK1/STAT6 reversed silymarin's protective effects, confirming a causal role of this pathway in the cellular context. Our in vitro data demonstrate that silymarin directly stimulates JAK1/STAT6 to drive M2 polarization and anti‑inflammatory responses. In vivo, we observed a correlation between pathway activation and neuroprotective benefits. Together, these findings provide a rationale for further exploring silymarin‑based therapies in SAH. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s10616-026-01073-w.

candidates.title: Fumarate Hydratase-Deficient Renal Cell Carcinoma in a Solitary Kidney: Diagnostic Pitfalls and Onco-Nephrology Constraints in an Older Adult With Chronic Kidney Disease.
candidates.abstract: Fumarate hydratase-deficient renal cell carcinoma (FH-dRCC) is a rare, aggressive subtype that is recognized as its own distinct entity in the 2022 WHO classification. It is frequently misclassified as papillary renal cell carcinoma (RCC). Older-onset disease and management in patients with a solitary kidney and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are not well characterized. A 76-year-old man with a remote right nephrectomy for clear cell RCC and stage 3b CKD presented with two to three years of progressive fatigue. Imaging of the solitary left kidney showed a 4.5-5.2 cm upper-pole mass with bulky retroperitoneal, mediastinal, and hilar adenopathy with multiple pulmonary nodules. Core biopsy findings were initially read as papillary RCC; however, the extensive metastatic burden appeared disproportionate to the relatively modest renal primary.  Re-review demonstrated loss of FH on immunohistochemistry, and tumor sequencing confirmed a pathogenic FH p.G397R missense variant with programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) tumor proportion score 20%, revising the diagnosis to FH-dRCC (cT1bN1M1). Cytoreductive nephrectomy was not pursued because of the patient's solitary-kidney status, baseline CKD, and disease burden. First-line nivolumab plus cabozantinib was selected; therapy was briefly held for immune-related uveitis, then resumed. This case highlights two important issues: metastatic burden disproportionate to primary tumor size - especially in tumors initially labeled papillary RCC - warrants pathology re-review with FH immunohistochemistry; and a solitary kidney with CKD reshapes the surgical and systemic-therapy calculus in FH-dRCC. Onco-nephrology input is valuable when balancing nephrotoxicity, contrast exposure, and disease-directed therapy.

candidates.title: GNAI2 activating variants and MAGIS syndrome: long-term endocrine and growth outcome.
candidates.abstract: Germline activating variants in the GNAI2 gene have recently been associated with MAGIS syndrome, characterized by midline malformations of the brain, anterior pituitary gland dysfunction, growth retardation, immunodysregulation, and skeletal defects. However, the full phenotypic spectrum, particularly regarding endocrine dysfunction, remains incompletely defined. We report on a 9.5-year-old male presenting with MAGIS syndrome due to a de novo GNAI2 (NM_002070.4):c.544A>C, p.(Thr182Pro) variant. He initially presented at 17 months with short stature and hypopituitarism. Pituitary MRI confirmed anterior pituitary hypoplasia with thin stalk and normal posterior pituitary. Long-term follow-up revealed suboptimal response to recombinant growth hormone therapy with persistent low IGF-1, profound prolactin deficiency, and evolving gonadotropin deficiency. He also had delayed developmental milestones, recurrent infections, chronic diarrhea, subclinical hypothyroidism, and skeletal abnormalities. Immunological evaluation showed low T-cell counts, inadequate antibody responses and no overt autoimmune features apart from infantile atopic dermatitis. This report details the longitudinal clinical, endocrine, and growth data in a patient with MAGIS syndrome harboring a GNAI2 p.Thr182Pro variant. It highlights the suboptimal growth response to GH with fluctuating height velocity and the development of additional endocrine abnormalities such as prolactin, thyroid dysfunction and suspected gonadotropin deficiency. Detailed phenotypic characterization in such cases is crucial for understanding this complex genetic disorder.

candidates.title: A Case of MEN 2A Syndrome With Bilateral Recurrent Pheochromocytoma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
candidates.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a neuroendocrine tumor arising from chromaffin cells and producing catecholamines. Due to the excessive release of catecholamines, these tumors can present with paroxysmal episodes of high blood pressure, headache, diaphoresis, and palpitations. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient who presented to the clinic with a history of headache, palpitations, and vomiting for two months. She was admitted for further investigations and management. Laboratory studies revealed elevated urinary and plasma catecholamine levels. Further work-up revealed bilateral adrenal masses diagnosed as pheochromocytoma and medullary thyroid cancer. The patient was diagnosed with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) type 2 and underwent bilateral laparoscopic adrenalectomy and total thyroidectomy with central and lateral neck dissection, and during surveillance, she was found to have recurrent pheochromocytoma. We also discuss the diagnosis and management of recurrent pheochromocytoma in MEN syndrome.

candidates.title: Integrated assessment of driving performance, eye movements, and cognitive function in obstructive sleep apnea: A pilot study.
candidates.abstract: Motor vehicle accident (MVA) risk is greater in patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), yet the functional domains most closely linked to driving-related impairment remain incompletely understood. This exploratory pilot study aimed to perform an integrated assessment of driving performance, eye movements, vigilance, and cognitive function in OSA and to examine their relationships with disease severity and treatment response. Adult drivers with suspected OSA underwent assessment using a driving simulator, Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT), eye-tracking, and the Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Battery (CANTAB). Participants with moderate-to-severe OSA (apnea-hypopnea index ≥20) who initiated continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy underwent re-evaluation after 6-12 months. At baseline, single-task reaction time in the driving simulator was positively correlated with apnea severity. In contrast, response accuracy under multitask plus steering conditions was associated with nocturnal hypoxemia (T90), suggesting differential contributions of apnea frequency and oxygen desaturation to driving performance. Eye-tracking parameters, including saccade amplitude and fixation duration, were significantly correlated with both driving performance and spatial working memory error scores. Following CPAP therapy, simple reaction times improved in both the driving simulator and PVT, whereas changes in multitasking performance and CANTAB measures were not statistically significant. Basic psychomotor speed was associated with OSA severity and improved following CPAP therapy, suggesting within-subject improvement of vigilance-dependent processes. In contrast, integrated oculomotor and executive function measures were more closely linked to complex driving performance, indicating that multidomain assessment may better characterize driving-related impairment in OSA. These findings provide preliminary evidence to guide future hypothesis-driven studies.
